## NEW THIS SCAN (2026-08-10) — Agent 365 + agent identity/publishing layer
Found by reading the Foundry BLOG (devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry), which names features the
whats-new roll-up omits, then following into the docs. **None of this has ever appeared in any
report from this monitor.** It is a second backlog recovery on the same primary-tier platform.

### Microsoft Agent 365 — GENERALLY AVAILABLE since May 1, 2026
learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/overview  (ms.date 2026-06-02, updated_at 2026-06-30)
Microsoft's enterprise **control plane for AI agents**. Treats agents as first-class Entra
identities via Entra Agent ID. GA for the Commercial segment on a per-user basis. Needs Microsoft
E5 (best) + at least one qualifying Agent 365 / M365 Copilot license.
Three pillars observe / govern / secure; five capabilities:
  - **Registry** — complete tenant inventory of ALL agents: Foundry agents, Copilot Studio agents,
    admin-registered agents, and **shadow agents discovered in the tenant**. Tracks ownership for
    governance + attestation. Companion surfaces: Agent registry, Registry sync, **Agent Map**.
  - **Access control** — Entra identity-based authorization, RBAC + ABAC, risk-based Conditional
    Access.
  - **Visualization** — explore connections between agents, people and data; real-time behavior
    monitoring.
  - **Interoperability** — gives agents access to M365 apps + org data; can connect to Work IQ.
  - **Security** — Microsoft Defender threat detection / behavior monitoring; Microsoft Purview
    information protection, DLP and compliance controls on agent activity and data.
Also: a set of **pre-integrated ecosystem partner agents** deployable straight from the M365 admin
center (third-party-agents).
Governance workflows: periodic access reviews, provisioning/deprovisioning lifecycle policies,
owner attestation for high-impact agents.

### Foundry ↔ Agent 365 integration
learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-365-integration
(ms.date 2026-06-05, updated_at 2026-07-11)
Two connection paths:
  - **Automatic registry sync** — published Foundry agents appear in the Agent 365 registry when
    subscribed.
  - **Autopilot publishing** — a Foundry **Hosted** agent can be published as an *autopilot*: an
    agent that acts autonomously on behalf of a user and **receives its own Entra Agent ID**. After
    publish + admin approval it lands in the Agent 365 registry and can be wired to Teams and other
    M365 surfaces.
Support matrix: Prompt agent = registry sync ✅ / autopilot ✅ / activity data ✅.
Hosted agent = registry sync ✅ / autopilot ✅ / activity data via A365 SDK (needs explicit config
+ Entra permissions for the Agent 365 observability service — how-to/grant-agent-365-permissions).
Enablement gates: (1) tenant needs >=1 M365 Copilot license AND enrollment in the **Frontier preview
program**; (2) a global admin enables Agent 365 in the M365 admin center, picks users/groups, and
accepts terms of service. Per-Foundry-resource logging is controlled by the **`agent365Config`
resource provider configuration**; no data flows without license + accepted ToS even if the ARM
property is enabled.
**Data residency**: Foundry follows the **Azure region** of the resource; Agent 365 follows the
**Entra tenant** storage location. Activity data crossing Foundry -> A365 moves between the two
residency models. Individual Foundry resources can opt out.

### Autopilot agents (from the Foundry blog + samples)
devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/whats-new-in-microsoft-foundry-june-2026/
A new agent *category*, public preview. Each autopilot gets its own **Entra Agent ID user account
with a productivity license, email, calendar, OneDrive and Teams presence**. Built for shared
spaces (Teams group chats), not 1:1 chat. Interaction model shifts from prompt->response to
**goal -> ongoing execution -> checkpoints -> collaboration**: it surfaces progress, requests
approvals and escalates to a human, natively inside Teams/M365. Reference implementation is the
**Workstream Manager** sample (tracks tasks, summarizes conversations into action items, chases
overdue work, surfaces risks; includes manager onboarding flows and access controls).

### Publishing an autopilot — provisioning footprint
learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/agent-365
(ms.date 2026-06-05, updated_at 2026-06-30). "Microsoft Agent 365 is generally available."
Creates: Foundry account + project, model deployment, hosted agent + agent version, Azure Container
Registry, **Azure Bot Service resource**, Application Insights + Log Analytics workspace. Submits an
autopilot request that creates an **agent blueprint** in the M365 admin center for approval.
Permissions: Azure **Owner** at subscription/RG scope; **Foundry User** or **Foundry Project
Manager** at project scope; **Owner/Contributor** at RG scope for Bot Service (Foundry-scoped roles
do NOT include `Microsoft.BotService/*`); **AI Administrator or Global Administrator** in the M365
admin center to approve. Requires `Microsoft.BotService` RP registration. Approval flow lands in
admin.cloud.microsoft -> agents -> requested; then Teams Developer Portal verification; then users
create an *instance* of the autopilot in Teams (Apps -> Agents for your team).

### NEW agent object model (replaces Agent Applications)
learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/migrate-agent-applications
(ms.date 2026-07-21, updated_at 2026-07-21)
Collapses **Agent Application** and **Agent Deployment** into the **Agent** object itself.
  - Before: Agent (data plane) + Agent Application (control plane) + Deployment (control plane) as
    separate objects. Unpublished agents SHARED the project's Entra agent identity + blueprint; a
    unique identity was only minted at publish.
  - After: only Agent objects. New properties: `id`, `name`, `versions`, **`agent_endpoint`**
    (stable endpoint), **`protocol_configuration`**, **`authorization_schemes`**,
    **`version_selector`**, **`blueprint`**, **`instance_identity`**, and **`agent_card`**
    (surfaces agent details + capabilities to consumers and to **A2A**).
  - Every newly created agent gets a unique **Entra Agent Blueprint + Entra Agent Identity BY
    DEFAULT, at creation**. BYO blueprint supported but not default.
  - Creating an agent is now the ONLY step needed to get a stable endpoint and unique identity.
    "Publishing" now means only distribution to M365/Teams channels.
Three agent types during transition, distinguished by `agent.identity` / `instance_identity`:
  **new** (non-null), **legacy** (null — shares project identity, backfilled with new properties but
  cannot be published to Teams/M365 via stable endpoint), and **published agents aka Agent
  Applications** (separate legacy resource).
No in-place upgrade for legacy agents — you must recreate the agent to get a unique identity.
Endpoint URL change: `/applications/{app}/protocols/openai` -> `/agents/{agent}/endpoint/protocols/openai/responses`.
Timeline: new model available; legacy Agent Applications still supported; legacy identity upgrade
gesture "coming soon"; Agent Application deprecation **planned**, end of support TBD.
Role assignments do NOT transfer from Agent Application identities to the new agent object.

### Agent Applications (legacy) — ARM resource detail
learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/agent-applications
(ms.date 2026-06-19, updated_at 2026-07-17)
ARM types: **`Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/projects/applications`** and
**`.../applications/agentDeployments`**.
Application properties: `displayName`, `baseUrl` (read-only dedicated endpoint), `agents`,
**`agentIdentityBlueprint`** (read-only), **`defaultInstanceIdentity`** (read-only),
**`authorizationPolicy`**, **`trafficRoutingPolicy`**, `provisioningState`, `isEnabled`.
Deployment properties: `displayName`, `deploymentId`, `state` (Starting/Running/Stopping/Failed/
Deleting/Deleted/Updating), `protocols`, `agents`, `provisioningState`, **`deploymentType`**
(`Hosted` | `Managed`), `minReplicas`, `maxReplicas`. Explicit start/stop APIs.
Protocols: **Responses** (OpenAI-compatible; stateless `POST /responses` only — `/conversations`,
`/files`, `/vector_stores`, `/containers` inaccessible) or **Activity Protocol** (Azure Bot
Service). Only one protocol at a time. Auth: Default (Azure RBAC, needs **Foundry User** or
`Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/AIServices/applications/invoke/action`) or **Channels (Azure
Bot Service)** — used automatically for M365/Teams/A365 autopilot publishing. **API key auth is NOT
supported.** Note: the **Foundry Agent Consumer** role does NOT grant Agent Application invoke.
>>> **"Foundry Agent Applications are not registered in the Microsoft Entra agent registry."** <<<
An explicit, documented discovery blind spot.
Publisher-pays cost model (publisher pays for deployed infra, not per call).

### Agent identity framework
learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity
(ms.date 2026-04-13, updated_at 2026-07-31)
  - **Agent identity** = a special **service principal** in Entra ID representing the agent at
    runtime. **Agent identity blueprint** = an Entra object governing a *class* of agent identities,
    used for lifecycle ops. `agentIdentityId` is the assignee for permissions.
  - Four-stage runtime OAuth 2.0 token exchange, fully automatic: blueprint authentication ->
    agent identity token issuance -> scoped token request against the downstream **audience** ->
    authenticated tool call. Audiences: storage.azure.com, logic.azure.com, cosmos.azure.com,
    graph.microsoft.com, vault.azure.net.
  - Blueprint credential types: **client secret**, **certificate**, or **federated credential
    (managed identity)** — the last is what Foundry provisions (trust to the project's managed
    identity, no stored secret). Blueprints can carry Graph permissions / delegated scopes.
  - Auth modes: **attended** (OAuth 2.0 on-behalf-of; agent limited to what the user consented to)
    and **unattended** (client credentials / app-only; governed only by the agent's own RBAC and
    Graph app permissions — no human involved).
  - Blueprint = type classification, enabling Conditional Access per agent *class*, bulk
    disable/revoke, and audit at scale.
  - Shared project identity for unpublished agents vs distinct identity once published.
    **Permissions do NOT transfer when you publish** — role assignments must be redone or tool
    calls fail with authorization errors.
  - Tenant-wide inventory: **Entra admin center -> Entra ID -> Agent ID -> All agent identities**,
    covering Foundry agents, **Copilot Studio agents** and others. Built-in controls there:
    Conditional Access, identity protection, network access, governance (expiration, owners,
    sponsors).
  - Tools currently supporting agent-identity auth: **MCP** (connection auth type
    `AgenticIdentityToken`, category `RemoteTool`) and **A2A** (`AgenticIdentityToken`, category
    `RemoteA2A`).
  - Identity lifecycle is tied to the project / agent application resource; deleting removes them.

### Foundry RBAC ROLE RENAME (carried on several pages)
**Azure AI User -> Foundry User; Azure AI Owner -> Foundry Owner; Azure AI Account Owner -> Foundry
Account Owner; Azure AI Project Manager -> Foundry Project Manager.** Role IDs and core permissions
unchanged; old names still visible in places while the rename rolls out. Any discovery or policy
keyed on role *names* will silently miss the renamed roles.
